correctness.rationale: The unitary transform in the two-site cell index gives the stated blocks. Their determinants are (ab/2)(cos(2π α)−cos(2π k/q)) in the supercritical regime. The leading coefficient and roots with multiplicities of T_q−1 give the exact determinant, including its sign. Each vanishing block has rank one; the two interior resonant frequencies are distinct, whereas the critical case has just k=0. Subcritical block determinants stay ≥1−a−b. The largest singular value is attained at k=0 by entrywise monotonicity after removing phases. At either zero the determinant has slope magnitude πab sin(2π α) and the other singular value tends to √S_*. A nearest sample gives an O(1/q) upper bound on the minimum, so every minimizing sample lies within O(1/q) of a root by the local two-sided linear bound and compactness away from the roots. The relative Taylor error there is O(1/q), even when the nearest distance is unusually small. This gives exactly the stated constant and the three approximation regimes. Transposition preserves all singular values.
residual_risks: No archived script was executed. The approximate Liouville parameter in the supplied check is only a finite real-number test, not evidence for Liouville behavior; the theorem for the exact parameter follows from the arithmetic proof.

value.rationale: For an elementary positive local blur, invertibility at every finite size does not imply even a polynomial conditioning bound. The result identifies the fixed phase that decides which resolutions are unusable and gives the sharp perturbation scale on the others. This is a useful explicit benchmark separating inverse-conditioning pathologies from one-step amplification and from FFT implementation effects.
residual_risks: The sharp law is for fixed exact parameters and exact arithmetic, not for coefficient rounding or algorithmic stability.
